summary:
Gender-affirming care in South Africa is concentrated in the major metropolitan centres, and the Free State has no documented concentration of its own. A trans visitor who needs hormone therapy or surgery while in the province should expect to travel outside it, paying private prices in the hundreds of thousands of rands or waiting on a long public list. No Free State-specific provider, waiting-time or funding data was identified.

No Free State-specific statute, provincial enforcement record, prosecution or documented incident involving a transgender person was identified. Policing, provincial hospitals, municipal facilities and the province's correctional centres operate under the national framework carried by the South Africa record, and for those matters the national assessment is the one a visitor should rely on.
tangentialFactors: A national custody ruling heard in Gauteng, Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre (Equality Court, case 2024/070075, judgment 10 November 2025), binds the Department of Correctional Services as a national department, so the remedies it orders for transgender inmates, among them state-funded gender-affirming hormone therapy and enforcement of the department's own standard operating procedures, reach correctional centres in the Free State. The case and its reasoning are carried by the South Africa record; compliance inside Free State facilities is not documented here.
localsOnly:
For residents the practical constraint is distance. Care is concentrated in the metropolitan centres, so Free State residents travel outside the province for hormone therapy and surgery, private treatment is priced in the hundreds of thousands of rands, and public waiting lists are long. No Free State-specific gender-affirming provider network, support service or provincial health policy on trans care was identified.

No Free State-specific protection, ombuds office or provincial programme addressing transgender residents was identified. The safeguards that exist are national instruments available anywhere in South Africa.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Free State-specific record of hate-crime prosecutions, police conduct or violence against transgender people was identified. Whether the Department of Justice's National Task Team, established in 2011, or the National Intervention Strategy for LGBTI Communities of April 2014 has any provincial implementation in the Free State is not sourced.

Bathroom and facility access: a 2024 analysis in PER/PELJ, 'Did the CPA Shut the Bathroom Door?', examines whether gender-segregated bathrooms excluding transgender and non-binary people amount to unfair discrimination under the Promotion of Equality and Prevention of Unfair Discrimination Act read with section 9 of the Constitution, and concludes that trans people do not in practice receive equal protection in facility access. No Free State venue, municipal or provincial policy on gender-segregated facilities was identified, so the position within the province is unresolved.

Health provision: whether Free State public hospitals and clinics offer gender-affirming hormone therapy, and what waiting times patients face, is not documented in the sources reviewed.
